title: Extract B: Marenia's economy loses momentum (fictional news report with Table 1)
text:
Marenia's economy loses momentum

Marenia's national statistics office confirmed on Friday that real output fell in Year 3, the first contraction for more than a decade. Officials blamed a 12% depreciation of the Marenian dollar during Year 2, which pushed up the cost of imported fuel, food and machinery, and a slump in orders from the country's largest export market. Consumer prices rose faster in Year 3 than in any year since the index was rebased. The central bank, which had held its policy rate at 2.0% for three years, raised it in two steps to 4.5% during Year 3, saying it was "determined to bring inflation back to the 2% target even at some cost to short-run growth". Business groups criticised the move, arguing that dearer borrowing would deepen the downturn, while the finance ministry said it was "considering all options", including a temporary cut in fuel duty and a public infrastructure programme. Manufacturing employment fell for a fifth consecutive quarter.

Table 1: Selected indicators for Marenia

| Indicator | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nominal GDP ($ billion) | 500.0 | 530.4 | 550.8 |
| GDP deflator (Year 1 = 100) | 100.0 | 102.0 | 108.0 |
| Consumer price index (Year 1 = 100) | 100.0 | 102.5 | 109.2 |
| Labour force (millions) | 20.0 | 20.5 | 21.0 |
| Unemployed (millions) | 1.00 | 1.23 | 1.68 |
| Population (millions) | 40.0 | 40.4 | 40.8 |
| Central bank policy rate (%, end of year) | 2.0 | 2.0 | 4.5 |
| Current account balance ($ billion) | -10.0 | -15.9 | -22.0 |

title: My draft answer (parts a to c)
text:
(a) Nominal GDP went from 530.4 to 550.8, so growth = (550.8 - 530.4) / 530.4 x 100 = 3.85%. The GDP deflator in Year 3 is 108, which means inflation was 8%. Real GDP growth = 3.85% - 8% = -4.15%, so the economy shrank by 4.15%.

(b) Unemployment rate = unemployed / population x 100 = 1.68 / 40.8 x 100 = 4.1%. This is still fairly low. One reason it has changed since Year 1 is that the population grew from 40.0 to 40.8 million, so there are more people looking for work and not all of them can find jobs.

(c) The central bank raised interest rates from 2% to 4.5%, which is a 2.5% increase. Higher interest rates mean people save more, so banks have more money to lend to firms, so investment rises and AD shifts to the right. Real GDP rises and the price level falls because there is more output in the economy. Diagram: AD1 moves to AD2 on the right.
